title: Jeremiah 46
paragraphs: ¹ The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations. ² Concerning Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt, which was stationed at the Euphrates River near Carchemish and was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah: ³ "Get your shields ready, both large and small, and march into battle. ⁴ Harness the horses; mount up, you cavalry! Take your positions with your helmets on. Polish your spears, put on your armor. ⁵ Why do I see them terrified and retreating? Their warriors are defeated, they flee in panic without looking back — there is terror on every side," declares the LORD.

⁶ "The swift cannot flee, the strong cannot escape. In the north by the Euphrates River they stumble and fall. ⁷ Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers swelling with water? ⁸ Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers swelling with water. She says, 'I will rise and cover the earth and destroy the city and all who live in it.' ⁹ Charge, you horses! Drive hard, you chariots! March forward, you warriors — men of Cush and Put who carry shields, men of Lydia who draw the bow. ¹⁰ But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Armies, a day of vengeance — vengeance on his enemies. The sword will devour until it is satisfied and drink its fill of blood. For the Lord GOD of Armies has a sacrifice in the north country by the Euphrates River."

¹¹ "Go up to Gilead and get medicine, O young woman, daughter of Egypt. But your many remedies will be of no use — there is no healing for you. ¹² The nations will hear of your disgrace; your cry will fill the earth. One warrior will stumble over another; together they will both fall. ¹³ This is the message the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to attack Egypt: ¹⁴ Announce it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol, proclaim it also in Memphis and Tahpanhes: 'Take your positions and prepare yourselves, for the sword will devour all around you.' ¹⁵ Why have your strong warriors been swept away? They could not stand their ground because the LORD pushed them down."

¹⁶ They stumble repeatedly, falling over each other. They say, "Get up! Let us go back to our own people and our homeland, away from the sword of the oppressor." ¹⁷ There they will exclaim: "Pharaoh king of Egypt is only a loud noise — he has let the right moment pass." ¹⁸ "As I live," declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies, "one is coming who is like Tabor among the mountains, like Carmel by the sea." ¹⁹ Pack your bags for exile, O daughter who dwells in Egypt, for Memphis will be laid waste, left in ruins with no inhabitant. ²⁰ Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a horsefly is coming from the north — it is coming.

²¹ Egypt's hired troops are like well-fed calves in a pen — they too will turn and run together; they will not stand their ground, for the day of their disaster has come upon them, the time of their punishment. ²² Egypt flees with a hiss like a snake; her enemies come marching in force and attack her with axes, like woodcutters. ²³ They will cut down her forest, declares the LORD, dense as it may be. They are more numerous than locusts — too many to count. ²⁴ Egypt will be put to shame; she will be handed over to the army of the north. ²⁵ The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to punish Amon the god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh and Egypt, and her gods and her kings — yes, Pharaoh and all who trust in him.

²⁶ I will hand them over to those who seek their lives — to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But afterward, Egypt will be inhabited again as in former times, declares the LORD. ²⁷ But do not be afraid, my servant Jacob; do not be dismayed, Israel. For I will surely save you from far away, your descendants from the land of their exile. Jacob will return and have peace and security, and no one will make them afraid. ²⁸ Do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, declares the LORD, for I am with you. I will completely destroy all the nations where I scattered you, but I will not completely destroy you. I will discipline you justly, but I will not let you go entirely unpunished.
